facts.text: Reginald the Frog warns that a little trickster creature called a Clurichen comes from the riverbanks into Brandonsford every night, up to no good, and that the party should stay away from wherever it goes.
facts.ended_how: removed: the Clurichen Naggeneen was caught and now hangs captive in a bag behind Quinn's bar (beat_20, beat_24, beat_26)
facts.classification: {"harm_origin":"external","negative_outcome_clarity_justification":"Reginald only says the creature is up to no good and to stay away; no particular harm is named.","negative_outcome_clarity":"low","outcome_severity_justification":"It is described as a little trickster, suggesting mischief rather than serious harm.","outcome_severity":"low","evidentiary_strength_justification":"Rests on a single warning from a talking frog, testimony of uncertain reliability.","evidentiary_strength":"medium","evidence_of_progression_justification":"Reginald says it comes into town every night, an ongoing pattern, but no harmful progression is shown.","evidence_of_progression":"medium","preventability_justification":"The party could follow the advice to avoid where it goes, though they do not know where that is.","preventability":"medium"}

facts.text: What does the Clurichen do when it comes into town each night?
facts.ended_how: answered: Naggeneen sneaks into the Golden Egg's basement to drink Quinn's alcohol (beat_21, beat_23)
facts.classification: {"question_basis":"Reginald's warning that the creature enters town nightly up to no good, without saying what it does, raises the question; no adventure want depends on it, so it is a possible revelation rather than an objective.","question_role":"revelation","goal_thread":"","grounding_justification":"A specific warning about nightly mischief clearly raises what the creature does.","grounding":"medium","investigative_depth_justification":"The answer would reveal a hidden nightly activity and its intent.","investigative_depth":"medium","narrative_payoff_justification":"Play has not tied the creature to other events, so the answer is mainly mildly interesting.","narrative_payoff":"low","investigative_potential_justification":"The party could watch the riverbanks or town at night or question Reginald and townsfolk.","investigative_potential":"medium","question_type":"open_ended"}

facts.text: Naggeneen, hung captive in a bag behind Quinn's bar, offers his pot of gold or a secret to whoever lets him go; Quinn holds him, and Sir Phidipaldi refused the offer on grounds of honor.
